equity_bridge.note: Judgment, not a filing figure. ~50% probability the Delaware Supreme Court appeal fails and the FTC clears the $2.35B deal, x ~$0.8B estimated excess of price over standalone value to Verisk (the company itself tried to walk away from the price in Dec-2025). Roughly -$3.1/share. Revisit when the appeal or the FTC Second Request resolves.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not computable: shareholders' equity swung from $2.8B (FY2021) to a $1.19B DEFICIT (2026-06-30) as $7B+ of debt-funded buybacks retired ~25M shares, so the house-default book-value anchor is meaningless here. Revenue CAGR used instead.
historical_growth.notes: FY2016-FY2021 revenue in the CSV is restated for the 2022 divestitures of Energy (Wood Mackenzie) and Financial Services, so the 5-year window is continuing operations. EPS 3-year CAGR (2.5%) is depressed by the FY2022 disposal gain in the base; the 3-year owner-FCF CAGR (16.3%) is flattered by FY2022's tax payments on those disposals -- the 5-year 7.6% is the cleaner read. Owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs track each other (SBC ~2.6% of revenue and stable), so SBC is not funding a growing share of reported growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Verisk's regulatory statistical-agent position and ~90% P&C penetration hold; the 2025-26 claims-volume softness was weather, and growth returns to ~6.5% in 2027-29 on pricing and new modules, fading to 3.5% by year 10, with adjusted margin creeping up ~40bps a year. AccuLynx is treated as a probability-weighted overpayment, not a growth driver.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI turns out to widen the moat: auditable, regulator-grade contributory data becomes the input every insurer's AI workflow needs, distributed through XactAI, Core Lines Reimagine and third-party assistants (Claude MCP connectors). Growth runs at 8% for four years with ~60bps/yr margin gains, and the market re-rates toward a premium compounder (22x terminal).
scenario_narratives.bear: AI commoditises the non-regulatory analytics layer, core-system vendors (Guidewire) bundle substitute data, and a soft P&C cycle plus quiet catastrophe years keep claims-linked revenue weak; growth stalls at 3-4%, AI-compute and talent costs compress margin ~1pp, leverage taken on for buybacks limits flexibility, and the business is capitalised at 15x as a slow-growth data utility.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Verisk is valued as a mature, subscription-heavy data franchise on fully SBC-expensed unlevered owner FCF at an 8% USD WACC, with the FY2026 year anchored to reaffirmed guidance and later years to the Investor Day 6-8% organic / 25-75bps margin framework. Book value is meaningless (debt-funded buybacks created an equity deficit), so the revenue CAGR is the growth anchor. Risk is charged through scenario paths and a bear-tilted 25/50/25 weighting, not a WACC premium.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI commoditisation of proprietary insurance data/analytics (the central multiple debate)
Claims-volume and soft-market cyclicality: four quarters of sub-target organic growth
AccuLynx: forced completion of a $2.35B deal Verisk tried to abandon; appeal pending at the Delaware Supreme Court, FTC Second Request open
Leverage: ~2.2x net debt/EBITDA after $1.9B of debt-funded H1-26 buybacks
Terminal value is ~64% of base EV; the 20x cap binds at an 8% WACC and 3% growth

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 155.94-250.20
data_sources.financials: VRSK_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, FY2009-Q1 2026); Q2-2026 10-Q (filed 2026-07-29, accession 0001437749-26-024749) for the 2026-06-30 balance sheet, debt table, ASR note and cover share count; Q2-2026 earnings release exhibit (accession 0001437749-26-024748) for FY2026 guidance and the adjusted-EBITDA definition; 8-K 2026-08-18 (AccuLynx appeal).

inputs.share_count_basis: 130,156,012 shares outstanding at 2026-07-24 (Q2-26 10-Q cover) plus ~0.09M dilutive awards (Q2-26 EPS note: 88,302) = 130.25M fully diluted. The February ($1.5B) and June ($200M) ASRs were finalised in July 2026; if the final share deliveries landed after 24 July the true count is ~1M lower (~+0.8% to per-share value), not taken. Held FLAT: SBC (incl. withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count too would double-charge it. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement: stock-based compensation $54.2M + net share settlement of taxes from RSAs/PSUs $26.7M (financing) = $80.9M. Verisk publishes no combined figure and its adjusted EBITDA does NOT add back SBC (Q2-26 release definitions), so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.85 -> cost of equity ~8.6%. Debt $4.47B at ~5.2% pre-tax (senior notes 3.6-5.75%) -> ~4.0% after tax. Market cap ~$21.3B, D/V ~17% -> WACC ~7.8%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; risk is carried in the scenario paths and weights, not a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost sits inside cost of revenues/SG&A and therefore inside EBITDA; operating lease liabilities ($143.6M) are NOT in net debt. Finance leases ($18.1M) are inside total debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, insurance data/analytics subscription business; Verisk is a data vendor TO insurers, not an insurer -- it carries no float or policy liabilities, so the BVPS/FCFE insurer routes do not apply). First valuation of VRSK; no prior DCF. BASE YEAR: FY2025 revenue $3,072.7M includes $68.0M from Verisk Marketing Solutions, sold Jan-2026; FY2026 growth of 4.6% is the guidance midpoint ($3.19-3.24B, reaffirmed at Q2-26 on 29-Jul-2026) and so already nets that disposal. MARGIN BASIS: the engine's EBITDA margin is PRE-SBC. Verisk's adjusted EBITDA is after SBC expense (it only adjusts earn-outs, disposal gains, equity-method items, deal fees, litigation reserves), so ebitda_margin = guided adjusted margin (56.0-56.5%) + SBC expense (~2.0% of revenue) = 58.25% for FY2026; the engine then deducts SBC incl. withholding taxes at 2.6%. D&A path is fixed-asset D&A only (guide $270-290M, ~8.7%); acquired-intangible amortisation ($60M) is excluded from the tax shield, a small conservatism. Capex guide $260-280M (~8.4%). Cash tax 24.5% = guided 23-26% book rate (FY2025 cash taxes were ~19% of pretax, not assumed to persist). WORKING CAPITAL: prepaid annual subscriptions -> deferred revenue grows with bookings; captured at 10% of the revenue increase. INTEREST: net debt company, so no interest income stripped; the engine values unlevered flows and deducts net debt at the 2026-06-30 balance sheet ($4,473.5M debt incl. finance leases less $551.4M cash). BUYBACKS: an aggressive repurchaser ($624M FY2025; $1.9B incl. ASRs in H1-26, debt-funded), so the flat count is funded, and over-funded. ACCULYNX: Delaware Chancery ordered specific performance on the $2.35B AccuLynx merger (Verisk appealed to the Delaware Supreme Court, 8-K 18-Aug-2026); no AccuLynx revenue or price is in the flows. A probability-weighted overpayment is deducted in equity_bridge instead (see there). Q2-26 actuals (10-Q filed 29-Jul-2026) are used for the balance-sheet anchors and guidance; Metrics.csv runs only to Q1 2026.

bear.narrative: The sub-6% organic run (four quarters) proves structural not weather: generative AI erodes the pricing power of non-regulatory analytics, Guidewire and core-system vendors embed competing data, a soft P&C market slows underwriting spend, and AI-compute and talent costs plus heavier capex give back margin. Growth settles at 3-4%, margins drift down ~1pp, and the market capitalises it as a slower data utility.

base.narrative: FY2026 at guidance midpoint (revenue $3.215B, adjusted EBITDA margin ~56.25%); organic growth returns to the low end of the 6-8% Investor Day range for 2027-29 on pricing (350-450bps over the cycle) and normal weather, then fades to 3.5%; adjusted margin expands ~40bps/yr (inside the 25-75bps target) to ~58.5% post-SBC.

bull.narrative: FY2026 at the top of guidance; AI is an accelerant: XactAI, the 25 Core Lines Reimagine modules and the Claude/MCP distribution channel lift wallet share, catastrophe-model demand compounds with insured losses, and growth runs at the top of the 6-8% range through 2029 with ~60bps/yr margin expansion.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: four consecutive quarters of organic growth below the 6-8% target, an unresolved AI-commoditisation debate that has de-rated the stock, and the AccuLynx specific-performance ruling against Verisk. Base 50% because guidance has been reaffirmed twice and Q2-26 showed 8.0% underlying subscription growth. Bull cut to 25% because it needs both a growth re-acceleration to the top of the range AND AI acting as a net accelerant -- two independent things going right.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
